'''Ekaterina Sedia''' (born July 9, 1970) is a [[Russians|Russian]] [[fantasy]] writer.<ref name="ekaterinasedia">{{cite web |url=http://ekaterinasedia.com/index.php/biography/ |accessdate=21 October 2013 |title=Ekaterinasedia.com » Biography |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029190330/http://ekaterinasedia.com/index.php/biography/ |archive-date=29 October 2013 |url-status=dead |df=dmy-all }}</ref> She immigrated to the United States and attended college in [[New Jersey]] to obtain her Ph.D.<ref name="locusmagazine">{{cite web| url=http://www.locusmag.com/2009/Issue04_Sedia.html |title=locus online: Ekaterina Sedia|last=Joyce |first=Graham|date= April 2009|publisher= |accessdate=24 October 2013}}</ref> Her most famous work is ''[[The Alchemy of Stone]]'', a steampunk novel that examines sexism and class bigotry.<ref name="Newitz, Annalee 2013">Newitz, Annalee. "A Living Doll Tries to Survive a Workers' Revolution in "The Alchemy of Stone"" Io9. N.p., n.d. Web. 24 Oct. 2013.</ref> Sedia's other novels include ''The Secret History of Moscow'', ''According to Crow'', ''Heart of Iron'', and ''[[The House of Discarded Dreams]]''. She has also written several short fiction stories, poems, and nonfiction books, as well as edited anthologies of short stories.<ref name="ekaterinasedia.com">{{cite web |url=http://ekaterinasedia.com/ |title=ekaterinasedia.com |publisher=ekaterinasedia.com |accessdate=2013-10-25 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024101244/http://ekaterinasedia.com/ |archive-date=2013-10-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> Several of her publications have been nominated for awards and/or have made a well-known reading list. In addition, Sedia was the editor for Jigsaw Nation and the [[World Fantasy Award]]-winning ''[[Paper Cities: An Anthology of Urban Fantasy]]''.<ref name="sfadb awards">{{cite web|last=Kelly|first=Mark|title=sfadb: Ekaterina Sedia Awards|url=http://www.sfadb.com/Ekaterina_Sedia|accessdate=14 October 2013}}</ref> In addition to writing, she teaches ecology and evolution courses as a professor at [[Stockton University]] in [[Galloway, New Jersey]].<ref name="SediaBlog">{{cite web |url= https://fishmonkey.blogspot.com/ |title=On summer, The Virgin Suicides, with some outfit pics. |last1=Sedia |first1=Ekaterina |date= September 2013 |accessdate=9 October 2013}}</ref>

==Background and early life==
Ekaterina Sedia was born on July 9, 1970  in [[Moscow, Russia]], as Ekaterina Holland.<ref name="ekaterinasedia"/> At age 21, Sedia moved to the United States to pursue advanced degrees. She currently teaches plant ecology and botany at [[Stockton University]] and lives in [[New Jersey]] with her husband Christopher Sedia and their cats.<ref name="locusmagazine"/> In her spare time, she blogs about fashion, food, cats, books, television, and feminism.<ref name="ekaterinasedia"/>

==Education==
Sedia did her undergraduate work at [[Moscow State University]].<ref name="locusmagazine" /> She later moved to Boston and worked at [[MIT]]’s Department of Brain and Cognitive Science as a research assistant.<ref>{{cite web|title=Interview|url=http://www.locusmag.com/2009/Issue04_Sedia.html|publisher=Locus Online|accessdate=October 20, 2013}}</ref><ref name="locusmagazine" /> After that she moved to New Jersey and went to graduate school at [[Rutgers University-Camden]], which is where she got her Ph.D. in ecology and evolution in 2001.<ref name="locusmagazine" /> Today she works at [[Stockton University]] teaching plant ecology and evolution.<ref name="Billectric Interview">{{cite web|title=Billectric Interview|date=30 September 2008|url=http://billectric.wordpress.com/2008/09/30/interview-with-ekaterina-sedia/}}</ref><ref name="SediaBlog" />

==Writing==
{{Main|Ekaterina Sedia bibliography}}Sedia has written novels, short stories, and essays, and has also edited several anthologies.<ref name="SediaCite">{{cite web|last1=Sedia|first1=Ekaterina|date=September 2013|title=Ekaterina Sedia|url=http://ekaterinasedia.com/|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131024101244/http://ekaterinasedia.com/|archive-date=24 October 2013|accessdate=26 October 2013|df=dmy-all}}</ref> Her work features [[Folklore of Russia|folklore]], [[fantasy]], [[urban fantasy]], and [[steampunk]] aesthetics. She has occasionally published under the name E. Sedia.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Summary Bibliography: Ekaterina Sedia|url=http://www.isfdb.org/cgi-bin/ea.cgi?50731|access-date=2021-12-05|website=www.isfdb.org}}</ref>

===Novels===

====''According to Crow'' (May 2005)====

In this story set in Sium, Josiah lives in a world where even though the war is over it is still not great times. The war had been over for seventeen years: however, there is no doubt the Meran Empire would expand. Josiah meets Caleb and they become friends. The two boys leave the country for fear of being persecuted and they find a strange world.  A war is about to happen and Josiah must choose sides and potentially betray his heritage.<ref>Sedia, Ekaterina. "Novels." Ekaterina Sedia. N.p., n.d. Web. 07 Oct. 2013.</ref>

====''The Secret History of Moscow'' (November 2007)====

''The Secret History of Moscow'' is a fantasy novel set in the underworld of capitalist Russia. Galina lives in Moscow with her sister who gives birth in a bathroom. She then turns into a jackdaw and flies away. At first Galina is reluctant to report anything because of her history of mental illness. She then meets an alcoholic artist named Fyodor who claims he knows where the bird people go. Galina finally
tells Yakov about this strange transformation and he too says he has seen something similar. Fyodor then takes them to a magical doorway to underground Moscow where creatures from Old Russian folklore live. They resurrect a dead body who then tells them his old boss might be responsible for the weird things that are going on.<ref>"The Secret History of Moscow." Kirkus Reviews 75.17 (2007): 895‐896. Academic Search Complete.</ref>

====''[[The Alchemy of Stone]]'' (July 2008)====

In ''[[The Alchemy of Stone]]'' skilled alchemist named Mattie, who is a living doll, finds herself in a conflict between gargoyles mechanics, and alchemists. The city is under threat of revolution and Mattie learns of secrets that could change the balance of power in the city. Loharri, Mattie's creator learns of this and this upsets him. He has the key to Mattie's heart literally and will do what it takes to stop her.<ref name="Newitz, Annalee 2013"/>

====''[[The House of Discarded Dreams]]'' (November 2010)====

''The House of Discarded Dreams'' is set in New Jersey and is considered urban fantasy.<ref>Penn, Joanna. "Writing Fiction. What Is Urban Fantasy Anyway?" The Creative Penn RSS. N.p., 3 Apr. 2013. Web. 09 Oct. 2013.</ref>  College student Vimbai moves out and away from her controlling mother. She moves into a house on the beach with two other roommates where strange things start to happen. Maya is followed by a pack of dog like animals and Felix has a pocket universe instead of hair. Vimbai's dead grandmother returns as a ghost and starts doing house work. The house one day floats off to sea and starts expanding. Vimbai must find a way home and on her journey she unexpectedly learns about herself culturally.<ref>"The House of Discarded Dreams." Publishers Weekly 257.23 (2010): 40. Academic Search Complete. Web. 15 Oct. 2013.</ref>

====''Heart of Iron'' (July 2011)====

''Heart of Iron'' takes place in Russia in 1852. Sasha an eighteen-year-old is enrolled into a university thanks to her aunt. At first, Sasha is concerned with sexism until she starts to notice that the Chinese students are disappearing. A boy with strange powers named Jack helps Sasha stop a kidnapping and this when she learns that a war could break out between China and Russia or China and England or both.<ref>"Heart Of Iron." Publishers Weekly 258.23 (2011): 29. Academic Search Complete. Web. 16 Oct. 2013.</ref>

===Editing work===

Sedia was an intern non-fiction editor for [[Clarkesworld Magazine]], in the fall of 2008.<ref name="ekaterinasedia.com"/>

She is also editor of the Award-winning ''[[Paper Cities: An Anthology of Urban Fantasy]]'' (2008),<ref name="strangehorizons1">{{cite web|url=http://www.strangehorizons.com/reviews/2008/10/paper_cities_ed.sh |accessdate=October 24, 2013 }}{{dead link|date=May 2016|bot=medic}}</ref> and other collections including ''Circus Fantasy: Fantasy Under the Big Top'' (2012), ''Jigsaw Nation'' (2006), and ''Running with the Pack'' (2010).<ref name="strangehorizons1" /><ref name="prime-books1">{{cite web |url=http://www.prime-books.com/shop/print-books/circus-fantasy-under-the-big-top-edited-by-ekaterina-sedia-2/ |title=Circus: Fantasy Under the Big Top edited by Ekaterina Sedia &#124; |publisher=Prime Books |date= |accessdate=2013-10-25 |archive-date=2013-10-29 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029192335/http://www.prime-books.com/shop/print-books/circus-fantasy-under-the-big-top-edited-by-ekaterina-sedia-2/ |url-status=dead }}</ref>

==Academic career==
Sedia is an associate professor of biology at [[Stockton University]], in [[Galloway Township, New Jersey|Galloway]], New Jersey.

Sedia specializes in the characteristics of the [[New Jersey Pine Barrens]] and how the population of [[lichen]]s, [[moss]]es, and [[grass]]es affect the forests and [[Ecological succession|the succession of the forest]]. She coauthored an influential paper on the differential effects of lichens, mosses, and grasses on respiration and nitrogen mineralization,<ref name="PaperOne">Ehrenfeld J.G., Sedia E.G., 2005. Differential effects of lichens, mosses and grasses on respiration and nitrogen mineralization in soils of the New Jersey Pinelands. Oecologia 144:1:137-147.</ref> how it promotes an alternate plant community,<ref name="PaperTwo">Ehrenfeld J.G., Sedia E.G. 2003. Lichens and mosses promote alternate stable plant communities in the New Jersey Pinelands. Oikos 100:3:447-458.</ref> and decomposition of litter in the New Jersey Pinelands.<ref name="PaperThree">Ehernfeld J. G., Sedia S. G. 2006. Differential effects of lichens and mosses on soil enzyme activity and litter decomposition. Journal of Biology and Fertility of Soils 43:2:177-189.</ref>
